source-integrity.provenance: Operating/financial, governance and supply-chain facts use SEC/issuer primary evidence; valuation/share-count uses independent S&P Global-derived StockAnalysis data.
source-integrity.freshness: Q2 2026 operating evidence, FY2025 20-F and 2026-09-23 valuation are current enough for T0 scoring.
source-integrity.duplicateOriginCollapse: Issuer releases and SEC mirrors are one economic origin and are not double-counted.
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: Independent valuation is distinct from issuer/regulatory evidence; operating facts remain issuer/regulatory provenance.
source-integrity.rawVsDerivedConsistency: Revenue acceleration, continuing losses, financing dependence and dilution are mutually consistent; no material unresolved contradiction.

evidenceClaims: Q2 2026 revenue was $18.1m versus $9.7m a year earlier, operating loss was $18.4m, liquidity was about $48.5m before approximately $30m gross July financing, and FY2026 guidance remained $67-$73m revenue with 2-3 new program wins.
FY2025 20-F documents Volkswagen, Mobileye and Daimler Truck programs, Fabrinet high-volume InnovizTwo manufacturing, contract-manufacturer expansion and broader InnovizSMART markets.
FY2025 20-F warns some key components are limited/single source, external semiconductor foundries are dependencies, and 2025 export-control changes forced alternative sourcing and mitigation cost.
FY2025 20-F states a majority-independent board, independent audit/compensation committees, shareholder-approved compensation policy and performance-linked CEO PSUs.
Independent 2026-09-23 market data showed $117.55m market cap, $104.74m enterprise value and roughly 288.03m shares outstanding, with shares up about 18% year over year.

thesisQuality.basis: Real OEM design wins, series-production experience and defense diversification establish a credible problem/adoption thesis, but durable economics remain unproven while losses and program-conversion uncertainty persist.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue nearly doubled year over year and guidance implies growth, but an $18.4m quarterly operating loss, shrinking pre-financing liquidity and recurring equity funding keep momentum in the weak-to-mixed band.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: About $117.55m market cap/$104.74m EV is low relative to current revenue and qualified OEM opportunities, creating upside asymmetry, but continuing losses and dilution prevent an 80+ assessment.

catalystScore.basis: FY2026 program-win guidance, defense follow-on potential and OEM/contract-manufacturing ramps are identifiable catalysts, but timing and volume conversion remain uncertain.

governancePower.basis: Majority-independent board, independent audit/compensation committees and performance-linked long-term CEO equity support adequate-to-strong governance; small-company financing dependence and shareholder dilution temper the score.

alignment2036.basis: Automotive autonomy, physical-AI sensing, robotics, traffic and defense/security perception address durable automation and safety needs across several markets.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: The InnovizTwo technology base is reused across automotive, defense/security, robotics and smart-infrastructure applications, though automotive programs still dominate economic scale.

bottleneckControl.basis: Automotive-grade qualification, in-house critical-component design and manufacturing know-how create barriers, but Innoviz does not control an irreplaceable sensing bottleneck and customer qualification remains external.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Defense and physical-AI diversification improve resilience beyond automotive timing, but loss-making economics and customer-program dependence remain material concentration risks.

substitutionResilience.basis: Automotive qualification and proprietary LiDAR design provide replacement friction, while competing LiDAR vendors and camera/radar/fusion architectures remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Contract-manufacturer expansion provides capacity options, but the 20-F explicitly identifies limited/single-source key components, external foundry dependence and export-control-driven sourcing disruptions.

pricingPower.basis: Tier-1 status can improve direct economics, but the 20-F explicitly describes substantial continuing OEM price-reduction pressure and lagged cost pass-through; durable pricing power is not demonstrated.

riskEvidence.basis: Material risks are cash burn/dilution, OEM program timing/concentration, limited/single-source components, foundry/geopolitical exposure and sensor substitution; low valuation partly reflects these risks.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability, current operating results, audited annual disclosures, governance, supply-chain dependencies and current independent valuation now cover all 12 components; program-level future economics remain explicit uncertainty.

scoreRecord.thesis: Innoviz has credible automotive-grade LiDAR qualification and expanding cross-market sensing applications at a depressed valuation, but the investment case remains constrained by loss-making economics, dilution and customer/supply-chain dependencies.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Cash burn and dilution can outrun OEM/defense volume conversion while substitutes and limited-source components pressure economics.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: FY2026 revenue/program-win execution, follow-on defense orders and volume conversion through contract-manufacturing ramps.

scoreBreakdown.note: Methodology 1.0 weighted component score; risk and confidence remain separate gated fields.

failedStrategy: Prior Alpha stopped on valuation, governance and supply-chain extraction despite lawful paths being available.
changedStrategy: Used current independent valuation plus direct 20-F governance/manufacturing/supplier disclosures and applied the machine-readable calibration anchors.

contradictions.claim: Record revenue and program traction versus continuing operating losses and equity financing.
contradictions.resolution: Both are supported; traction raises opportunity but does not imply self-funded economics.

unknowns: Future OEM SOP timing and mature unit economics remain uncertain.
Exact component-level alternate-source coverage is not fully disclosed.
